conditions.name: Generalized Anxiety
conditions.description: Persistent excessive worry with somatic tension. Ayurvedic understanding relates to Chittodvega with Vata–Pitta involvement. Yoga therapy, pranayama and meditation have supportive evidence alongside professional psychological care.

conditions.name: Hypertension
conditions.description: Persistently elevated blood pressure. Ayurvedic correlation includes Raktagata Vata. Approaches include DASH-style dietary patterns, sodium reduction, regular aerobic activity, stress management and prescribed antihypertensives.

conditions.name: Insomnia
conditions.description: Difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep. Ayurveda correlates with Anidra/Nidranasha. Sleep-hygiene, CBT-I and yoga-based relaxation (yoga nidra) are evidence-aligned measures.

conditions.name: Knee Osteoarthritis
conditions.description: Degenerative joint disease of the knee with pain and stiffness. Correlated with Sandhivata. Exercise therapy, quadriceps strengthening and weight management form the core; topical applications may offer adjunct comfort.

conditions.name: Obesity / Overweight
conditions.description: Excess adiposity measured by BMI and waist circumference. Asian-Indian cutoffs (waist >90 cm men, >80 cm women; BMI ≥23 overweight) apply. Ayurveda names this Sthaulya — a Medo-dhatu disorder.

conditions.name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
conditions.description: Chronic metabolic disorder characterised by insulin resistance and hyperglycaemia. In Ayurveda, correlated with Madhumeha (Prameha spectrum). Management combines medical nutrition therapy, physical activity, prescribed medication and structured monitoring.
